source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 893 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 893 was established by Ordinance No. 29063, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 26, 2013. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 893 is established on property located north of Bent Tree Forest Drive between the Dallas North Tollway and Knoll Trail Drive. The size of PD 893 is approximately 2.53 acres. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this district:

(1) BLADE SIGN means a sign projecting perpendicularly from a main building facade, visible from both sides, and made of rigid or soft materials.

(2) STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residence.

(3) TANDEM PARKING means one parking space in front of another parking space, making it necessary to pass through one parking space to gain vehicular access to the other parking space.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 893A: development plan. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. Development plans may be submitted in phases or for any portion of the Property. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

(1) Residential uses.

-- Multifamily. -- Retirement housing.

(2) Utility and public service uses.

-- Local utilities. -- Tower/antenna for cellular communication. [Limited to a mounted cellular antenna.] (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator.

(c) The following accessory uses are permitted by SUP only:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Amateur communication tower. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard.

(1) Except as provided in this section, minimum front yard is:

(A) 15 feet along the Dallas North Tollway.

(B) 20 feet along Bent Tree Forest Trail.

(C) 25 feet along Knoll Trail Drive.

(2) Balconies, bay windows, awnings, patios, and entryways may project up to five feet into the front yard.

(3) Blade signs may be located anywhere within the front yard.

(4) Stoops, retaining walls, transformers and other utility equipment, benches, pots, raised planters, sculptures, cabanas, and other decorative landscape items may be located anywhere within the front yard.

(b) Side yard. No minimum side or rear yard.

(c) Density. Maximum density for all residential uses is 276 dwelling units or suites.

(d) Floor area. No maximum floor area.

(e) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 75 feet.

(2) The following structures may project a maximum of 12 feet above the maximum structure height:

(A) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.

(B) Mechanical equipment room.

(C) Visual screens that surround roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum coverage is 75 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground structures are not.

(g) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(h) Stories. No maximum number of stories. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.109. OFF-STREET PARKING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Tandem parking. Tandem parking is allowed in areas that are restricted to resident use only. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials. The use of high quality, cold-hardy, and drought-tolerant plant materials is required.

(c) Designated landscape areas.

(1) Definitions.

(A) LANDSCAPE BUFFER STRIP means the designated landscape area that serves a buffer function where a residential adjacency exists.

(B) LANDSCAPE SITE AREA means at least 20 percent of a lot, including at least 50 percent of the required front yard. GENERAL PLANTING AREA means at least 50 percent of the landscape site area, including at least 25 percent of the required front yard. SPECIAL PLANTING AREA means at least 20 percent of the general planting area, including at least five percent of the required front yard.

(C) PARKWAY PLANTING AREA means at least 20 percent of the parkway.

(2) Minimum planting requirements. The minimum planting requirements for designated landscape areas are as follows:

(A) Landscape site area. No minimum planting requirements for portions of the landscape site area that are outside of the general planting area.

(B) General planting area. The general planting area must contain shrubs, vines, flowers, or ground cover vegetation. All plants in this area must be recommended for local area use by the building official.

(C) Special planting area. The special planting area must contain shrubs or vines that are recommended for local area use by the building official. Turf grass and ground cover are not counted toward meeting these minimum planting requirements. Initial plantings must be able within three years to cover a minimum of 75 percent of the special planting area and grow to a minimum height of 24 inches. There must be at least one plant for each four square feet of the special planting area unless a landscape architect recommends an alternative planting density as part of a landscape plan that the building official determines is capable of satisfying the minimum coverage requirement.

(D) Parkway planting area.

(i) The parkway planting area must contain trees along Knoll Trail Drive and Dallas Parkway, and turf grass, flowers, or ground cover vegetation that are recommended for local area use by the building official for all street frontages.

(ii) Initial plantings must be able within three years to cover a minimum of 75 percent of the parkway planting area.

(iii) An owner or tenant is not required to comply with this subparagraph to the extent that compliance is made impossible due to rejection of the private license application for the parkway or city council’s revocation of the private license.

(3) Soil depth.

(A) There is no minimum soil depth for portions of the landscape site area that are outside of the general planting area.

(B) The minimum soil depth for portions of the general planting area that are outside of the special planting area is 18 inches.

(C) The minimum soil depth for the special planting area is 24 inches unless restricted by underground utilities.

(D) The minimum soil depth for trees in the parkway planting area is 30 inches.

(4) Pavement.

(A) No pavement other than pavement for pedestrians and non-motorized vehicles is permitted in the designated landscape site areas.

(B) No pavement other than permeable pavers is allowed in the general planting area, special planting area, and parkway planting area.

(d) Street trees.

(1) Knoll Trail Drive and Dallas North Tollway. One large tree must be provided for each 40 feet of street frontage. These trees must be located within 30 feet of the projected street curb. The trees may be planted in the parkway provided that all private licensing requirements of the city code and charter are met. An owner or tenant is not required to comply with this subsection to the extent that compliance is made impossible due to rejection of the private license application for the parkway or city council’s revocation of the private license.

(2) Bent Tree Forest Drive. Due to the existence of underground utilities, street trees are not required. Trees existing before June 26, 2013 and within 30 feet of the curb may qualify for site trees. Tree replacement is not required if a tree within 30 feet of the curb is removed because it interfered with the construction or maintenance of a public utility.

(3) Minimum size. Street trees must each have a minimum height of 14 feet and a minimum caliper of three and one-half inches.

(4) Spacing. Street trees must be spaced as uniformly as practicable, but no more than 40 feet on center.

(5) Site trees. Street trees planted in the parkway may be counted as site trees.

(6) Tree mitigation. Street trees planted in the parkway may be counted toward the tree replacement requirement for the property.

(e) Maintenance.

(1) All landscaping required under this section must be irrigated and drained by automatic irrigation and permanent drainage systems installed to comply with industry standards, except as restricted by a public utility. The building official may authorize an alternative irrigation that is adequate to maintain the plants in a healthy, growing condition.

(2) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.112. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Multifamily use.

(1) A maximum of three blade signs are permitted in the following locations:

(A) A maximum of one blade sign is permitted along the Dallas North Tollway frontage.

(B) A maximum of one blade sign is permitted along the Bent Tree Forest Drive frontage.

(C) A maximum of one blade sign is permitted along the Knoll Trail frontage.

(2) Blade signs may project into a required yard.

(3) Each sign must be at least 12 feet above grade.

(4) Illuminated blade signs along Bent Tree Forest Drive and Knoll Trail are prohibited. Illumination of the blade sign along the Dallas North Tollway is limited to internal lighting.

(5) No blade sign may project above the top of an occupied floor or the highest point of a parking structure.

(6) Maximum effective area for a blade sign along the Dallas North Tollway is 92 square feet. Maximum effective area for blade signs on Bent Tree Forest Drive and Knoll Trail is 68 square feet each. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Building Facade Materials
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.113. BUILDING FACADE MATERIALS.

(a) In general. To ensure compatibility with surrounding uses, facades facing a public right- of-way must be at least 70 percent masonry, excluding windows, entrances, and ingress and egress points. Masonry includes stone, brick, concrete, hollow clay tile, decorative concrete blocks or tile, glass block, other similar building materials, or a combination of these materials. For purposes of this subsection, stucco is considered masonry but Exterior Finish Insulations System (EFIS) materials are not.

(b) Facade design elements. Facades facing public rights-of-way must incorporate at least three of the following design elements. The cumulative length of these design elements must extend for at least 50 percent of the facade’s horizontal length.

(1) A repeating pattern of wall recesses and projections, such as bays, offsets, reveals, or projecting ribs that have a relief of at least eight inches.

(2) A repeating pattern of pilasters projecting from the facade wall by a minimum of eight inches or architectural or decorative columns.

(3) Enhanced exterior light fixtures such as wall sconces, light coves with concealed light sources, ground-mounted accent lights, or decorative pedestal lights.

(4) Trim, molding, or accent elements using decorative contrasting colors or decorative neon lighting equal to at least five percent of the area of the facade.

(5) Decorative metal not to exceed 20 percent of any one facade. The use of corrugated metal panels is prohibited.

(c) Facade changes. Facades must have a one or more of the following changes:

(1) Changes of color, texture, or material, either diagonally, horizontally, or vertically, at intervals of not less than 20 feet and not more than 100 feet.

(2) Changes in plane with a depth of at least 24 inches, either diagonally, horizontally, or vertically, at intervals of not less than 20 feet and not more than 100 feet.

(d) Entrance design elements. At least three of the following design elements are required at the primary entrance, so that the primary entrance is architecturally prominent and clearly visible from the abutting street:

(1) Architectural details such as arches, friezes, tile work, murals, or moldings.

(2) Integral planters or wing walls that incorporate landscaping or seating.

(3) Enhanced exterior light fixtures such as wall sconces, light coves with concealed light sources, ground-mounted accent lights, or decorative pedestal lights.

(4) Arcades, awnings, canopies, covered walkways, or porticos.

(5) Prominent three-dimensional features, such as belfries, chimneys, clock towers, domes, spires, steeples, towers, or turrets. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Except as provided in this subsection, a temporary leasing office may operate on the Property for up to 180 days after a building permit is issued. If construction of the residential uses has not been completed within that 180 days, the building official may grant additional 30-day-extensions for the temporary leasing office.

(b) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29063)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-893.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 29063)
